messages.author: b6689a9004e926b9
messages.subject: Multigroup comparison with sam
parts:
Hello there,
I was wondering if some of you already tried to run a multigroup comparison with the sam () function? 

I had to switch from a common SEM (which was fine regarding the fit measures) to factor score regression due to a small sample (N = 301) compared to the  high number of variables in my model, which made a multigroup comparison impossible. I discovered the sam function due to the need for a Croon correction. I did manage to run the sam function without any problem and it resulted in very similar results compared to my former latent model. I wanted to proceed with the multigroup comparison and ended up with a warning:
 
"Fehler in lavimplied$cov[[g]] : Indizierung außerhalb der Grenzen"
In English it is basically: Error in lavimplied$cov[[g]] : Indexing out of bounds

This is a really strange error, as I couldn't really find it elsewhere, just in cases where columns or rows are indicated in a syntax, which do not exist. 

I did use the normal lavaan command "group = ". Is there another command for it or maybe a problem with using the approach for a  multigroup comparison? Thank you so much in advance!

My original sam code was as following: 
fit.fsr <- sam(model = elfi_LF, data = myData2, cmd = "sem", missing = "fiml", se="twostep", group="zufall",  sam.method = "Croon", output = "lavaan")

Thank you so much for your help! 
Best regards

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup comparison with sam
parts:
> "Fehler in lavimplied$cov[[g]] : Indizierung außerhalb der Grenzen"
> In English it is basically: Error in lavimplied$cov[[g]] : Indexing out
> of bounds
>
> This is a really strange error,

Indeed. It works for me. For example:

HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9

visual ~ speed + textual
'
fit <- sam(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group = "school")

So there must be something funny with either the data or the model.
Could you send me your data (or a snippet of your data) and a short R
script that reproduces your error message? I will then investigate.

Yves.
